characters.name: Jesus
characters.note: Central figure of the Gospel; born in Bethlehem, raised in Nazareth, teaches and heals in Galilee and Judea, crucified in Jerusalem and raised.

characters.name: Joseph
characters.note: Husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus; a carpenter who receives angelic dreams (1:18-2:23). Not the same as Joseph of Arimathea.

characters.name: Mary
characters.note: Mother of Jesus, betrothed to Joseph; appears in the birth narrative and with her son and brothers (12:46, 13:55).

characters.name: King Herod
characters.note: King of Judea who seeks the child Jesus and orders the killing of boys in Bethlehem; dies before Joseph returns from Egypt. Distinct from Herod Antipas.

characters.name: the wise men
characters.note: Eastern visitors who follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gifts (2:1-12).

characters.name: an angel of the Lord
characters.note: Messenger who speaks to Joseph in dreams (1:20, 2:13, 2:19) and to the women at the tomb (28:2-7).

characters.name: John the Baptizer
characters.note: Preacher in the Judean wilderness who baptizes Jesus; imprisoned and beheaded by Herod Antipas (14:3-12). Not John the apostle.

characters.name: the Pharisees
characters.note: Religious leaders who repeatedly oppose or question Jesus.

characters.name: the Sadducees
characters.note: Religious party who question Jesus about the resurrection and join the Pharisees in testing him.

characters.name: the scribes
characters.note: Teachers of the law who debate with Jesus and join the chief priests against him.

characters.name: the devil
characters.note: Tempts Jesus in the wilderness and is accused by the Pharisees of being the source of Jesus's power.

characters.name: Simon Peter
characters.note: Fisherman from Capernaum, first of the twelve disciples; walks on water, confesses Jesus as Christ, and denies him three times. Not Simon the Zealot.

characters.name: Andrew
characters.note: Brother of Simon Peter and fisherman, one of the first four disciples.

characters.name: James son of Zebedee
characters.note: Fisherman and one of the first disciples, brother of John; present at the transfiguration. Not James son of Alphaeus.

characters.name: John the apostle
characters.note: Son of Zebedee and brother of James, a disciple; present at the transfiguration and Gethsemane. Not John the Baptizer.

characters.name: Zebedee
aliases: the father of James and John
characters.note: Father of James and John, a fisherman mending nets with his sons when Jesus calls them (4:21).

characters.name: Matthew
characters.note: Tax collector called to follow Jesus (9:9); one of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.note: One of the twelve who betrays Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and later hangs himself.

characters.name: Philip
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3. Not Philip the tetrarch.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3.

characters.name: Bartholomew
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3; named only in lists.

characters.name: James son of Alphaeus
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3; named only in lists.

characters.name: Thaddaeus
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3; named only in lists.

characters.name: Simon the Zealot
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:4; named only in lists.

characters.name: Herod the tetrarch
characters.note: Ruler of Galilee who hears of Jesus, executes John the Baptizer at Herodias's request, and later mocks Jesus. Distinct from King Herod the Great.

characters.name: Herodias
characters.note: Wife of Herod's brother Philip who urges the execution of John the Baptizer.

characters.name: the daughter of Herodias
characters.note: Dances before Herod and asks for John's head on a platter (14:6-11).

characters.name: Caiaphas
characters.note: High priest who presides over the council that condemns Jesus.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate
characters.note: Roman governor who questions Jesus and orders his crucifixion.

characters.name: Barabbas
characters.note: Prisoner released instead of Jesus.

characters.name: the chief priests and elders
characters.note: Jerusalem's religious leaders who plot against Jesus and bribe the guards.

characters.name: the soldiers
characters.note: Roman soldiers who mock, flog and crucify Jesus and guard the tomb.

characters.name: the centurion
characters.note: Roman officer whose servant Jesus heals (8:5-13); distinct from the centurion at the crucifixion.

characters.name: the centurion at the cross
characters.note: Officer who watches the crucifixion and declares Jesus the Son of God (27:54). Possibly the same as the Capernaum centurion but not identified as such.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathea
characters.note: Rich disciple who buries Jesus in his new tomb (27:57-60). Not Joseph husband of Mary.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
characters.note: Woman who watches the crucifixion, the burial, and goes to the tomb on the first day.

characters.name: Mary, mother of James and Joses
characters.note: Woman at the crucifixion and the tomb, mother of James and Joses; distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus.

characters.name: Simon of Cyrene
characters.note: Man compelled by soldiers to carry Jesus's cross.

characters.name: Simon the leper
characters.note: Host at Bethany where a woman anoints Jesus (26:6).

characters.name: the woman with the alabaster jar
characters.note: Woman who anoints Jesus's head at Bethany (26:7).

characters.name: the woman with the discharge of blood
characters.note: Woman healed by touching Jesus's garment (9:20-22).

characters.name: the Canaanite woman
characters.note: Woman from Tyre and Sidon whose daughter is healed (15:22-28).

characters.name: a ruler
characters.note: Synagogue ruler whose daughter Jesus raises (9:18-25).

characters.name: the leper
characters.note: Man healed of leprosy on the mountainside (8:2-4).

characters.name: the paralytic
characters.note: Paralyzed man carried on a bed and forgiven and healed (9:2-8).

characters.name: the two demon-possessed men
characters.note: Two men living among the tombs in the country of the Gergesenes (8:28-34).

characters.name: the rich young man
characters.note: Man who asks what good thing to do for eternal life and goes away sad (19:16-22).

characters.name: the two blind men
characters.note: Blind men healed near Jericho or in Galilee (9:27-31, 20:30-34).

characters.name: the disciples
characters.note: Jesus's followers as a group.

characters.name: the multitudes
characters.note: Large crowds who follow Jesus, hear him, and sometimes shout for his crucifixion.

characters.name: the mother of the sons of Zebedee
characters.note: Mother of James and John who asks for places beside Jesus (20:20).

characters.name: a lawyer
characters.note: Scribe who asks Jesus which commandment is greatest (22:35).

characters.name: the guards at the tomb
characters.note: Soldiers who see the angel and report to the chief priests (28:11-15). Grouped with soldiers.

characters.name: the two robbers
characters.note: Two men crucified beside Jesus who revile him (27:38, 44).

characters.name: Moses
characters.note: Appears with Elijah at the transfiguration (17:3).

characters.name: Elijah
characters.note: Appears with Moses at the transfiguration; the crowd thinks Jesus calls him at the cross.

characters.name: Abraham
characters.note: Named in the genealogy and in teaching; mentioned only.

characters.name: King David
characters.note: Named in the genealogy and as the son of David title; mentioned only in most episodes.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.note: Town where Jesus is born and where Herod orders the killing of children.

locations.name: Jerusalem
aliases: the city of the great King
locations.note: Holy city with the temple; site of the temple confrontations, the trial, and the crucifixion.

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.note: Town in Galilee where Joseph and Mary settle with Jesus.

locations.name: Egypt
locations.note: Place of refuge for the holy family.

locations.name: the Jordan
locations.note: River where John baptizes and Jesus is baptized.

locations.name: the wilderness of Judea
locations.note: Desert where John preaches and Jesus is tempted.

locations.name: an exceedingly high mountain
locations.note: Place where the devil shows Jesus all the kingdoms of the world.

locations.name: Capernaum
locations.note: Galilean town on the sea where Jesus lives; Peter's house is there.

locations.name: the sea of Galilee
locations.note: Lake where the fishermen work, the storm occurs, and Jesus walks on the water.

locations.name: the country of the Gergesenes
locations.note: Region across the sea where the demon-possessed men are healed and the pigs drown.

locations.name: the mountain
locations.note: Hillside where the sermon on the mount is preached (chapters 5-7).

locations.name: the temple
locations.note: Temple in Jerusalem; site of cleansing, teaching, and the veil torn at the crucifixion.

locations.name: the Mount of Olives
locations.note: Hill east of Jerusalem where Jesus teaches about the end and is later arrested at Gethsemane.

locations.name: Gethsemane
locations.note: Garden on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prays and is arrested.

locations.name: the court of the high priest
aliases: the palace of the high priest
locations.note: Where Jesus is interrogated and Peter denies him.

locations.name: the Praetorium
locations.note: Headquarters of Pilate where Jesus is mocked and flogged.

locations.name: Golgotha
locations.note: Site of the crucifixion outside Jerusalem.

locations.name: Joseph's tomb
aliases: a new tomb cut in the rock
locations.note: Rock tomb where Jesus is laid and later found empty.

locations.name: Bethany
aliases: the house of Simon the leper
locations.note: Village near Jerusalem where Jesus stays, is anointed, and camps.

locations.name: Caesarea Philippi
locations.note: Region where Peter confesses Jesus as Christ.

locations.name: Jericho
locations.note: City on the road to Jerusalem where blind men are healed.

locations.name: Galilee
locations.note: Northern region where Jesus grows up and carries out much of his ministry.

locations.name: Tyre and Sidon
aliases: the region of Tyre and Sidon
locations.note: Gentile region where the Canaanite woman comes from.

locations.name: the tomb
locations.note: Where the women and the guards encounter the angel.

brief.tone: Reverent and luminous in the miracles and birth scenes, grave and sorrowful through the passion, with austere moral weight in the teaching discourses.
depiction_rules: Show Jesus as central and always identifiable; avoid depicting God the Father directly, use a voice from the cloud or light.
Angels appear as luminous human-like messengers, not winged cherubs drawn from later tradition unless the scene calls for it.
Depict the Holy Spirit as a dove in the baptism scene only, as the text describes.
The crucifixion may be shown but without gratuitous gore; the veil torn and the darkness are depicted as signs, not spectacle.
Parables are shown as realistic scenes of rural and town life of the period rather than allegorical symbols.
Avoid antisemitic caricature of Pharisees, scribes and crowds; show them as individuals with varied expressions.

era.name: First-century Roman Judea and Galilee
era.people: Jewish villagers, fishermen, shepherds, tax collectors, Roman soldiers and officials, Pharisees and priests in traditional dress; Gentiles from Tyre, Sidon and Syria appear in some scenes.
era.dress: Tunics and cloaks with fringed garments, head coverings, sandals, linen and wool; Roman soldiers in armor and tunics; priests in linen robes; women with veils.
era.buildings_and_objects: Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs, village synagogues, the Jerusalem temple with courts and veil, marketplaces, vineyards, threshing floors, fishing boats and nets, oil lamps, clay jars, tombs cut in rock.
era.technology: No gunpowder, printing or clocks; oil lamps, boats with sails and oars, hand mills, ox carts, coins such as denarii and shekels. Writing exists on scrolls and parchment.
